academic_translation:
If you have no attachment to impurity,
Why do you embrace in your lap another—
A cage of bones bound by sinews,
Plastered with the mud of flesh?
translation: If you are not attached to filth, why do you hug another person? They are a cage of bones tied together. They are covered with the mud of flesh.

academic_translation:
You yourself contain much impurity,
Which you constantly make use of;
And yet for other bags of filth as well,
You desire them out of greed for impurity.
translation: You are full of filth yourself. You carry it around all the time. Yet you still want other bags of filth. You desire them out of greed for filth.

academic_translation:
Saying, "I delight in this flesh,"
If you desire to touch and look at it,
How can you desire the flesh
Which is of an insentient nature?
translation: You say, 'I love this flesh.' You want to touch and look at it. But how can you desire this flesh? It is naturally without a mind.

academic_translation:
That mind which you desire
Cannot be touched or seen,
And that which can be is not consciousness;
What is the use of that meaningless embrace?
translation: The mind you want cannot be seen or touched. The part you can touch is not awareness. So what is the point of that useless hug?

academic_translation:
Another's body is of the nature of impurity—
Not realizing this is not a great wonder;
But that you yourself are impurity itself—
Not realizing this is a great wonder!
translation: Another person's body has the nature of filth. It is not surprising if you do not realize this. But you yourself are filth itself. It is a great wonder that you do not realize that!

academic_translation:
Having abandoned a fresh lotus
Opened by the rays of a cloudless sun,
With a mind attached to impurity,
Why do you delight in a cage of filth?
translation: You leave behind a fresh lotus opened by the bright sun. Your mind is attached to filth. Why do you find joy in a cage of filth?

academic_translation:
If you do not wish to touch a patch of ground
Smeared with impurity,
How can you wish to touch the body
From which that arose?
translation: If you refuse to touch a patch of ground smeared with filth, how can you want to touch the body it came from?

academic_translation:
If you have no attachment to impurity,
Why do you embrace another in your lap
Who arose from an impure field
And was produced by that seed?
translation: If you do not like filth, why do you hold someone in your lap who grew from an unclean field and was made by that seed?

academic_translation:
You do not desire even a tiny filth-worm
That has arisen from impurity,
Yet you desire a body whose nature is much impurity
And which was born from impurity.
translation: You do not want even a tiny worm born in filth. Yet you want a body that is full of filth and born from filth.

academic_translation:
Not only do you not disparage
Your own impurity,
But out of greed for impurity,
You also desire another bag of filth.
translation: You do not even hate your own filth. But out of greed for filth, you also desire another bag of filth.

academic_translation:
Even pleasant things like camphor,
Or cooked rice and vegetables,
Once put into the mouth and spat out,
Make even the ground impure and foul.
translation: Think of nice things like camphor, cooked rice, or vegetables. Once you put them in your mouth and spit them out, they make the ground foul.

academic_translation:
If you doubt such impurity as this,
Even though it is plainly evident,
The bodies discarded in the charnel grounds—
Look at those other impurities as well.
translation: If you still doubt this is unclean, even when it is easy to see, look at the bodies left in the place of the dead. Look at those other unclean things, too.

academic_translation:
If the skin is peeled away from it,
Great terror will arise;
Even knowing this, how can joy arise
In that very same thing once again?
translation: If the skin is peeled away from it, you will feel great fear. Since you know this, how can you feel joy for that same thing again?

academic_translation:
That scent smeared upon the body, too,
Is sandalwood and the like, not anything else.
Because of that scent of another,
Why do you have attachment to another?
translation: The smell rubbed on the body is just sandalwood and things like that. It is nothing else. Because of that smell of another, why do you have clinging to another?

academic_translation:
If it is naturally foul-smelling,
Is it not better to have no attachment to it?
Those in the world who pointlessly crave,
Why do they smear sweet scents upon it?
translation: If it naturally smells bad, isn't it better to have no clinging to it? Why do people in the world who crave for no reason rub sweet smells on it?

academic_translation:
But if the sweet scent is sandalwood,
What originates from the body here?
Because of the scent of another,
Why do you have attachment to another?
translation: But if the sweet smell is sandalwood, what actually comes from the body here? Because of the smell of another, why do you have clinging to another?

academic_translation:
If, with long hair and nails,
Yellowish teeth with filth, and imbued with the smell of mud,
The nature of the body
Is terrifying indeed when naked,
translation: If it has long hair and nails, dirty yellow teeth, and the smell of mud, the nature of the body is truly scary when naked.

academic_translation:
Like a weapon that harms oneself,
Why do you make efforts to tend to it?
Through the efforts of those deluded regarding the self,
This earth is completely agitated by madmen.
translation: Why do you work so hard to care for it, like a weapon that hurts you? Through the efforts of people confused about the self, this earth is completely stirred up by madmen.

academic_translation:
Having seen nothing but skeletons,
If you feel revulsion in the charnel ground,
Do you delight in the charnel ground of the village,
Pervaded by moving skeletons?
translation: If you feel sick seeing only skeletons in the place of the dead, why do you like the village? The village is also a place of the dead. It is filled with moving skeletons.

academic_translation:
Even that which has thus become impure
Cannot be obtained without a price.
From accomplishing that purpose comes exhaustion,
And harm in hell and so forth.
translation: Even things that are impure cost a price to get. Working for that goal just makes you tired. It also brings harm in hell and other places.

academic_translation:
Since a child cannot amass wealth,
When coming of age, what happiness is there in this?
If life is exhausted by amassing wealth,
Once old, what can one do with sensual desires?
translation: A child cannot gather wealth. When they grow up, what happiness is there in this? If you spend your whole life gathering wealth, you will get old. What can you do then with your desire for pleasure?

academic_translation:
Some wretched lustful people,
Utterly exhausted by a full day's work,
Return home, and their exhausted bodies
Sleep like corpses.
translation: An unhappy person full of desire works all day and gets completely tired out. They come home, and their tired bodies sleep like dead bodies.

academic_translation:
Some, afflicted by traveling abroad
And suffering from going far away,
Though longing for their wives and children,
Do not see them even for years.
translation: Some people travel to other places and experience the suffering of going far away. They long to see their wives and children. But they do not see them for years.

academic_translation:
Utterly deluded, though desiring their own benefit,
For whatever purpose they even sell themselves,
Without obtaining that, they are driven
By the wind of others' meaningless work.
translation: Some people are completely confused. They want to help themselves, so they even sell themselves for a goal. But they do not get what they want. They are just blown around by the wind of other people's meaningless work.

academic_translation:
Some sell their own bodies,
And, powerless, are put to work by others;
Even when their wives give birth,
It happens just anywhere, at the foot of a tree or in the wilderness.
translation: Some people sell their own bodies. They have no power and must work for others. When their wives have babies, it happens just anywhere. It might be at the foot of a tree or out in the wild.

academic_translation:
Fools deceived by sensual desire,
Wishing to survive and thinking, "I will make a living,"
Enter into battle despite fearing the loss of their lives,
And go into servitude for the sake of profit.
translation: Fools are tricked by desire for pleasure. They want to survive and think, "I will make a living." They go into battle even though they fear losing their lives. They become servants just to make a profit.
Sometimes a person full of desire gets their body cut apart. Some are stuck on the sharp points of stakes. Short spears pierce others. You can even see some being burned.

academic_translation:
Through the torments of accumulating, guarding, and losing,
Wealth should be known as endless ruin.
Those who are distracted by attachment to wealth
Have no opportunity to be freed from the suffering of existence.
translation: Gathering, guarding, and losing wealth brings pain. You should know that wealth causes endless ruin. People get distracted by clinging to wealth. Then they have no chance to be free from the suffering of life.

academic_translation:
For lustful persons, these and so forth
Are the many disadvantages, and the enjoyment is slight,
Just as beasts that pull a cart
Eat only a few mouthfuls of grass.
translation: A person full of desire faces these and many other drawbacks. Their enjoyment is very small. They are just like animals pulling a cart. Those animals only eat a few mouthfuls of grass.

academic_translation:
For the sake of that slight enjoyment,
Which is not rare even for beasts to accomplish,
This perfect leisure and endowment, so difficult to find,
Is destroyed by those tormented by karma.
translation: People destroy this free and fortunate life, which is so hard to find. They do this just for a tiny bit of enjoyment. Even animals can easily get that small pleasure. These people are hurt by their own actions.

academic_translation:
Sensual desires will certainly perish
And cause one to fall into hell and so forth.
For the sake of what is not great, at all times,
Whatever wearisome hardship has occurred—
translation: A desire for pleasure will certainly fade away. It causes a person to fall into hell and other bad places. We go through so much tiring hardship all the time for something that is not even great.

academic_translation:
If, by merely a ten-millionth fraction of that
Hardship, Buddhahood is accomplished,
For a lustful person, compared to the conduct of awakening,
The suffering is greater, yet there is no awakening.
translation: A tiny fraction of that hardship could bring us to the state of a Buddha. A person full of desire goes through suffering worse than the way of acting for awakening. Yet they get no awakening at all.

academic_translation:
If one considers the suffering of hell and so forth,
For sensual desires, weapons,
Poison, fire, precipices,
And enemies cannot even serve as examples.
translation: Think about the suffering in hell caused by a desire for pleasure. Weapons, poison, fire, steep cliffs, and enemies are not nearly as bad. They cannot even be used as examples.

academic_translation:
Having thus become weary of desire,
One should generate joy for solitude
Within peaceful forests
Empty of disputes and afflictions.
translation: Once you grow tired of desire, you should feel joy for solitude. Go into the peaceful forests. They are completely empty of arguments and troubling emotions.

academic_translation:
The fortunate ones, in delightful fine dwellings of broad stone slabs
Cooled by moonlight and sandalwood,
Fanned by the silent, peaceful forest breeze,
Pace while contemplating the benefit of others.
translation: Lucky people rest in lovely places made of wide stone slabs. They are cooled by moonlight and sandalwood. A quiet, peaceful forest breeze blows on them. They walk around and think about how to help others.

academic_translation:
In empty houses, at the foot of trees, and in caves,
Staying wherever and for as long as one desires,
Having abandoned the suffering of possessing and guarding,
One lives carefree, without dependence.
translation: They stay in empty houses, under trees, and in caves. They stay wherever they want for as long as they like. They leave behind the suffering of owning and guarding things. They live a carefree life without depending on anything.

academic_translation:
Acting independently and without attachment,
Unconnected to anyone at all,
Whatever happiness of contentment one enjoys,
That is difficult even for Indra to find.
translation: If I act on my own without clinging, I am not tied to anyone at all. The joy of being happy with enough is hard even for Indra to find.

academic_translation:
Through these and other such aspects,
Having reflected on the good qualities of solitude,
With conceptual thought fully pacified,
One should meditate on bodhicitta.
translation: By thinking about these things, I see the good qualities of solitude. When my busy thinking is completely calm, I should meditate on the awakening mind.

academic_translation:
The equality of self and others
One should first strive to meditate upon;
Since they are equal in happiness and suffering,
All should be protected like oneself.

locked_terms.use: seeing self and others as equal

translation: First, I should try hard to meditate on seeing self and others as equal. Since everyone is equal in happiness and suffering, I should protect everyone just like myself.

academic_translation:
Although the divisions of hands and so forth are many,
Just as they are one as a body to be fully protected,
Likewise, diverse wandering beings, with their happiness and suffering,
Are all one in equally desiring happiness, like oneself.
translation: A body has many parts, like hands, but it is protected as one whole body. In the same way, there are many different beings with their own happiness and suffering. But they are all one in wanting happiness just like me.
